titel: Basics of the flat-rate withholding tax
kurz: How the tax burden is made up of the special rate of 25%, the solidarity surcharge and church tax, and why the bank withholds the tax directly.

bloecke.md:
Until the end of 2008, capital income was taxed very differently depending on its type. Interest was subject to the personal tax rate, that is, up to 45% for high incomes. Dividends fell under the half-income method (Halbeinkünfteverfahren), under which only half was taxable. Price gains were completely tax-free after a holding period of twelve months. Investors who waited that long therefore paid no tax at all on increases in value.

Since 1 January 2009, a uniform special rate of 25% has applied to income from capital assets, regardless of other income (Section 32d(1) EStG, Income Tax Act). In return, the speculation period (Spekulationsfrist) was abolished. Since then, price gains have been taxable no matter how long the securities were held in the portfolio. An exception still applies today to shares acquired before 1 January 2009. Their price gains do not fall under the new rule (Section 52(28) sentence 11 EStG). For fund units, this grandfathering was restricted in 2018.

The tax rate is a separate rate and is not part of the progressive scale. On €1,000 of interest, a trainee therefore pays the same percentage as a board member. That was the declared intention of the legislator. A low tax rate that is easy to collect was intended to keep capital in the country.

bloecke.text: Better 25% of x than 42% of nothing.

bloecke.md:
## Capital income covered

Section 20 EStG distinguishes between two groups. Section 20(1) covers current income, that is, dividends (no. 1), income from investment funds (no. 3), interest on bank balances and bonds (no. 7) and income from certain life insurance policies (no. 6). Section 20(2) covers the capital itself, that is, gains from the sale of shares, bonds, certificates and derivative transactions (Termingeschäfte). Since 2018, gains from the sale of fund units have also belonged to Section 20(1) no. 3 as investment income (Section 16(1) no. 3 InvStG, Investment Tax Act).

Income that does not fall under Section 20 EStG is taxed under other rules and at other rates. Rental income is income from letting and leasing (Section 21 EStG) and is subject to the personal tax scale. Gains from gold, cryptoassets and collectibles count as private disposal transactions (private Veräußerungsgeschäfte) under Section 23 EStG, for which a separate holding period applies. The term “capital income withholding tax” (Kapitalertragsteuer) almost always refers only to the narrower scope of Section 20 EStG.

## Tax base

On a sale, it is the gain that is taxed. Section 20(4) sentence 1 EStG defines it as the sale proceeds less the expenses directly and materially connected with the sale, and less the acquisition costs. The order fee on purchase increases the acquisition costs; the order fee on sale reduces the proceeds. Both lower the gain and thus the tax.

Other costs do not reduce the tax. Section 20(9) EStG expressly excludes the deduction of the income-related expenses (Werbungskosten) actually incurred. Custody fees, specialist literature, seminars, asset management fees and interest on a securities loan therefore do not reduce the tax base. They are replaced solely by the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 per person (€2,000 for joint assessment). How it works and why it is not taken into account in the tax deduction without an exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) is covered in the next lesson.

When 100 shares are bought at €40.00, an order fee of €9.90 is incurred. The acquisition costs are therefore €4,009.90.

Three years later, the 100 shares are sold at €55.00. That comes to €5,500.00 less an order fee of €11.90.

The taxable gain is 5,500.00 − 11.90 − 4,009.90 = €1,478.20.

With the saver's allowance used up and without church tax, the tax is 1,478.20 × 26.375% = €389.87525. For the solidarity surcharge, fractions of a cent are disregarded (€20.32 instead of €20.32525), so the bank withholds €389.87. After tax, €1,088.33 remains.

The custody fees of €60 from these three years play no role for tax purposes. They reduce the return but not the tax base.

bloecke.erklaerung: The formula is set out in Section 32d(1) sentence 4 EStG. Without creditable foreign tax, it simplifies to e/(4+k). It follows from the equation S = 0.25 × (e − k × S). Under Section 32d(1) sentence 3 EStG, the tax is reduced by 25% of the church tax attributable to the capital income, so church tax reduces its own tax base. It is not deductible as a special expense (Sonderausgabe) under Section 10(1) no. 4 EStG. Solving for S gives S = 0.25e / (1 + 0.25k) = e / (4 + k).

bloecke.md: Church tax of 9% increases the total burden by only 1.62 percentage points, from 26.375% to 27.995%. Per €1,000 of income, the bank withholds €16.19 more, even though €22.00 of church tax is paid. The difference results from the lower capital income withholding tax and the lower solidarity surcharge. A blocking notice (Sperrvermerk) filed with the Federal Central Tax Office (BZSt) by 30 June (Section 51a(2e) EStG) saves no tax. It merely shifts the church tax into the tax return, where it creates an obligation to file.

## Tax deduction by the bank

The flat-rate withholding tax is deducted at source and not assessed by the tax office. The person liable for the tax is the investor, as the creditor of the capital income. The tax is withheld and paid over, however, by the “paying agent” (auszahlende Stelle), in practice the custodian bank (Sections 43 and 44 EStG). The tax withheld within a month must be paid over to the tax office by the tenth day of the following month (Section 44(1) sentence 5 EStG). This happens without names being given, so the tax office only sees totals and no individual investors.

The bank does not have to ask for the church tax rate. Once a year, it retrieves the church tax deduction indicator (Kirchensteuerabzugsmerkmal) automatically from the Federal Central Tax Office. The solidarity surcharge of 5.5% is also withheld. The exemption threshold (Freigrenze) under which the vast majority of people have paid no solidarity surcharge on their income tax since 2021 does not apply to the deduction of capital income withholding tax. The Federal Constitutional Court (BVerfG) confirmed the surcharge as constitutional in its judgment of 26 March 2025 (2 BvR 1505/20).

This procedure results in the **final withholding effect** (Abgeltungswirkung). For capital income that has been subject to capital income withholding tax, income tax is settled by the tax deduction (Section 43(5) EStG). This income does not have to be included in the tax return. That is convenient, but it leads many investors to forgo, for years, refunds to which they are entitled.

bloecke.titel: Exceptions to the final withholding effect
bloecke.md:
The special rate does not apply without exception. Section 32d(2) EStG excludes cases in which the difference between the tax rates could otherwise be exploited by deducting the expense at a rate of up to 45% and taxing the income at 25%. The exceptions are:

- Loans between related parties, if the debtor deducts the interest as income-related expenses or business expenses (no. 1a)
- Shareholder loans where the shareholding is 10% or more (no. 1b)
- Back-to-back financing via an intermediary bank (no. 1c)

In these cases, the personal income tax scale applies. In addition, there is no final withholding effect for capital income from business assets or for capital income on which no German tax has been deducted, for example with a foreign broker. Income without German tax deduction must be declared (Section 32d(3) EStG). Investors who deliberately fail to meet this obligation are evading tax (Section 370 AO, Fiscal Code). If the declaration is omitted through gross negligence, this constitutes reckless understatement of tax (leichtfertige Steuerverkürzung), an administrative offence under Section 378 AO.

## Taxation of nominal income

The flat-rate withholding tax makes no adjustment for inflation. It is levied on the nominal income, even if nothing of it is left after deducting inflation. In October 2026, this can be shown with current figures. The ECB deposit facility rate has been 2.50% since 16 September, and the German inflation rate was 3.3% in September. Of 2.50% interest, 1.84% remains after 26.375% tax. In real terms, that amounts to a loss of purchasing power of around 1.4% a year, and tax was still levied on the interest beforehand.

From this, a rule of thumb can be derived that is easy to check. Because only 73.625 cents of every euro of income reach the investor, the nominal interest rate must be at least inflation ÷ 0.73625 for purchasing power to be preserved. At 3.3% inflation, that is 4.48%. Interest-bearing investments have rarely reached this threshold in the past two decades.

bloecke.titel: Real return before and after tax (illustrative calculation)
bloecke.unter: At 3.3% inflation, the threshold for preserving purchasing power after tax is a nominal interest rate of around 4.5%; without tax, it is 3.3%.

bloecke.md:
1. Read the tax certificate. It shows capital income withholding tax, solidarity surcharge and church tax separately and is the only way to check what the bank has paid over.
2. Check the church tax indicator. After you leave the church, the bank continues to deduct church tax until the next annual retrieval date is reached. Church tax withheld in excess can only be reclaimed via the tax return.
3. Secure the acquisition data and keep the purchase contract notes permanently. If the bank lacks the acquisition data, it uses a flat 30% of the sale proceeds as the tax base under Section 43a(2) EStG. With small gains, this results in a multiple of the correct tax.

German income tax is designed as a synthetic tax. All types of income are added together and taxed uniformly on a progressive scale. The special rate for capital income departs from this principle. With taxable income of €80,000, the marginal tax rate is 42%, whereas additional interest income is taxed at 25%.

There are three arguments for this departure. The first concerns the mobility of capital. Before 2009, considerable sums were moved to countries without reporting to the tax authorities, so that in effect only investors who left their money in Germany paid the tax. The second concerns the prior tax burden, because distributed company profits have already been taxed at company level with corporation tax and trade tax (Gewerbesteuer). The third concerns the taxation of nominal values. Here the state also taxes illusory gains that stem only from inflation.

The counter-argument is that the automatic exchange of information between tax authorities has undermined the first argument, because foreign accounts are largely transparent today. As a result, the tax burdens earned income more heavily than investment income. The question is politically disputed. Abolishing or raising the flat-rate withholding tax is not provided for in the current coalition agreement.

mitnehmen: The special rate of 25% plus a 5.5% solidarity surcharge on it comes to 26.375% in total, or with church tax 27.82% (at 8%) or 27.995% (at 9%).
Through the formula e/(4+k), church tax reduces its own tax base and therefore increases the total burden, net, by only around 1.4 to 1.6 percentage points.
What is taxed is the gain, that is, the proceeds after deducting acquisition costs and order fees; ongoing custody costs and specialist literature do not reduce it (Section 20(9) EStG).
The bank withholds the tax at source and pays it over by the 10th of the following month without naming the investor, which settles the income tax (Section 43(5) EStG).
The tax is levied on nominal income, so at 3.3% inflation a nominal interest rate of around 4.5% is needed to maintain purchasing power.

begriffe.text: Separate tax rate of 25% for income from capital assets (Section 32d(1) EStG). It replaces the personal, progressive income tax scale.

Form in which the flat-rate withholding tax is collected. The paying agent, usually the custodian bank, withholds the tax and pays it over (Sections 43 and 44 EStG). The investor remains the person liable for the tax.
Once tax has been deducted at source, the income tax on the income is settled (Section 43(5) EStG), so the income no longer has to be declared. Exceptions are governed by Section 32d(2) EStG.

For capital income, income-related expenses actually incurred, such as custody fees or specialist literature, are not deductible (Section 20(9) EStG). They are replaced solely by the saver's allowance.

Coded information on religious affiliation that banks retrieve automatically once a year from the Federal Central Tax Office (Section 51a EStG). A blocking notice only prevents the retrieval; the church tax is still owed.
